tier_reason: Raised from C (first-party bellard.org table only) to A on the third-party nordlow/compiler-benchmark run: the harness is public (MIT; the script that produced the 2026-09-29 table is in history at commit 5712a50, flags unchanged at HEAD), the flags are fixed in that script (gcc/clang: -Wall -Wextra plus -fsyntax-only, -c or -o main, no -O so default -O0; tcc: -c -o /dev/null, -c or -o main, no other flags), the compiler versions are printed in the table (tcc 0.9.28rc, gcc 16.2.1, clang 22.1.8), and the CPU, OS and date are stated (AMD Ryzen AI 7 350, Arch Linux, as of 2026-09). Checked: Build links for all three compilers and Compile links for none; each cell is the minimum wall-clock time of 5 repetitions (time.perf_counter around Popen with psutil polling every 10 ms) divided by 40,000 generated functions; there is no #include in the generated file; and only the compiler exit code and stderr are checked, never the built binary's result. The workload is synthetic and the harness is noisy (14 concurrent pinned tasks, Build below Compile in the published table), which is recorded in the caveats and does not lower the tier. The exact tcc mob commit is not recorded.

corrections.claimed_speedup: nordlow/compiler-benchmark (README table of 2026-09-29, commit 5712a50; per-function minimum of 5 runs over 40,000 generated functions): Build [us/f] tcc 0.9.28rc 2.6 vs gcc 16.2.1 500.7 vs clang 22.1.8 60.3, about 193x faster than gcc -O0 and 23x faster than clang -O0 (derived from page data); Compile [us/f] tcc 3.5 vs gcc 732.5 vs clang 123.3, about 209x and 35x (derived from page data); Check [us/f] tcc 2.9 vs gcc 18.2 vs clang 15.4, about 6.3x and 5.3x (derived from page data), although tcc's Check row does full code generation into /dev/null while gcc and clang only run -fsyntax-only. The previous published run (the table that commit 5712a50 replaced) had Build tcc 3.6 vs gcc 805.8 vs clang 85.3 us/f, about 224x and 24x (derived from page data). First-party bellard.org figure: TinyCC 0.9.22 compiles, assembles and links the Links browser in 2.27 s (859,000 lines/s, 29.6 MB/s) vs GCC 3.2 -O0 in 20.0 s (98,000 lines/s, 3.4 MB/s) on a 2.4 GHz Pentium 4, 'about 9 times faster than GCC' (8.8x, derived from page data). The TinyCC README says 'Compiles and links about 10 times faster than gcc -O0'.
corrections.baseline: GCC at -O0 (gcc 16.2.1 in compiler-benchmark, GCC 3.2 in the bellard.org table); also Clang 22.1.8 at -O0
corrections.compiler_and_flags: compiler-benchmark script at commit 5712a50, with the same flags at HEAD: gcc 16.2.1 gets -Wall -Wextra; clang 22.1.8 gets -Wall -Wextra -fno-color-diagnostics -fno-caret-diagnostics -fno-diagnostics-show-option. Both then get -fsyntax-only (Check), -c (Compile) or -o main (Build), with no -O flag, so they run at default -O0. tcc 0.9.28rc is a mob-branch snapshot installed as the Arch package by provision.sh; its exact commit is not recorded. It gets -c -o /dev/null (Check), -c (Compile) or -o main (Build), with no warning or optimization flags. All three link in Build (gcc and clang through the system linker, tcc with its built-in linker); none links in Compile. bellard.org: TinyCC 0.9.22 vs GCC 3.2 -O0; no script or flags are published beyond that.
corrections.hardware: compiler-benchmark: AMD Ryzen AI 7 350, which the README labels '(8+8) @ 5.09 GHz'. It is a 28 W Krackan Point laptop part with 4 Zen 5 cores (up to 5.0 GHz) and 4 Zen 5c cores (up to 3.5 GHz), 16 threads. Arch Linux; the README says 'as of 2026-09' and the table was committed on 2026-09-29 (5712a50). bellard.org: 2.4 GHz Pentium 4 (TinyCC 0.9.22 was tagged 2004-11-08; GCC 3.2 dates from 2002).
corrections.workload: compiler-benchmark default run (--function-count=200 --function-depth=200 --run-count=5). Each repetition writes one generated C file: 40,000 one-line 'long f(long x) { return x + ... + const; }' functions in 200 call chains of depth 200, plus a main that calls the 200 chain heads and returns the sum. There is no #include or other prefix. Times are wall clock (time.perf_counter around subprocess.Popen, with psutil polling every 10 ms at the default --sample-rate=100). Each cell is the minimum of 5 repetitions divided by 40,000 (us per function). Absolute minimums: Build tcc about 0.10 s, clang 2.4 s, gcc 20.0 s; Compile tcc 0.14 s, clang 4.9 s, gcc 29.3 s (derived from page data). bellard.org: the Links browser source, 76,936 lines including headers, of which 1,950,947 lines (67.2 MB) are actually compiled; real time covers compile, assemble and link.
corrections.stars_or_usage: About 3.0k stars and 570 forks on the GitHub mirror (github.com showed 3,000 on 2026-10-07; 3038 at the 2026-09-24 check). The mirror describes itself as an 'Unofficial mirror of mob development branch' of repo.or.cz/tinycc.git. The V language bundles TCC binaries for fast development builds.
corrections.caveats: This supersedes the earlier note that a gcc -O0 baseline caps the entry at C. The tier now rests on a public third-party harness, with -O0 recorded as a caveat. The workload is synthetic: a single translation unit of arithmetic call chains with no #include. The benchmark README itself warns that real-world build times are 'heavily driven by header parsing (#include), package/module resolution, standard library footprint, and cross-crate/module parallelism, none of which are exercised by isolated arithmetic trees'. gcc and clang run at their default -O0 (plus -Wall -Wextra, which tcc does not get), so the lead holds only against unoptimized builds. The 193x Build gap over gcc is about 20x TinyCC's own 'about 10 times faster than gcc -O0' claim. It comes almost entirely from gcc's code generation on this one huge translation unit: gcc Check 18.2 vs Compile 732.5 us/f (derived from page data). The same Check-to-Compile jump does not appear in the bellard.org multi-file 8.8x. tcc's Check row emits code into /dev/null, while gcc and clang only run -fsyntax-only. The harness is noisy. In the 2026-09-29 table Build is lower than Compile for all three compilers (gcc 500.7 vs 732.5, clang 60.3 vs 123.3, tcc 2.6 vs 3.5 us/f), even though Build does strictly more work. Between the two published runs, clang Compile moved from 83.5 to 123.3 (+48%) and gcc Build from 805.8 to 500.7 (-38%) (derived from page data). At commit 5712a50 the script ran len(cpus)-2 tasks at once (14 on this 16-thread part), each pinned by worker index to one logical CPU, on a 28 W laptop chip that mixes 5.0 GHz Zen 5 and 3.5 GHz Zen 5c cores. Pinning to performance cores only arrived in a 2026-10-06 commit, after this run. The tcc-vs-clang Build ratio still stays at 23-24x across both runs. Polling every 10 ms adds up to about 10% to tcc's roughly 0.10 s builds but almost nothing to gcc's 20 s builds, so it understates tcc's lead. tcc's output is not validated. The harness checks only the compiler exit code and stderr, and it runs each built binary 5 times with output discarded, never checking its exit status or sum. Run time is reported only as speed: tcc 113 vs gcc -O0 98 vs clang -O0 155 us/f, with nothing at -O2. The exact tcc mob commit is not recorded; the table shows only 0.9.28rc. The script has changed since the run (work directory moved to /tmp, core selection, table layout), so reproducing the table needs the script at commit 5712a50. compiler-benchmark is a single-maintainer repo (nordlow, 166 stars, MIT). The bellard.org 8.8x figure is first-party, has no published script, and uses TinyCC 0.9.22 against GCC 3.2 -O0 on a Pentium 4. bellard.org was EGRESS_BLOCKED here, so the figure was re-confirmed from a search snippet and the 2026-09-24 verifier's reading. The GitHub repo is an unofficial mirror of the repo.or.cz mob branch. The last tagged release is release_0_9_27 (2017-12-12), and mob's VERSION reads 0.9.28rc, so the measured code is available only from mob, not from a release. COPYING is LGPL-2.1 and the README says TCC is distributed under the LGPL. A RELICENSING file lists authors who agree to MIT-style terms for their own contributions; it does not relicense the whole tree.
